szoveg_eredeti:
The workshop will take place as part of Hour of AI 2026, a global initiative aimed at making artificial intelligence more accessible to students and teachers through free and inclusive learning activities. The initiative is aligned with UNESCO’s AI competency framework for teachers, which promotes the development of skills to understand, use and teach these technologies through a human-centred, ethical and pedagogical approach.

During the workshop, participants will explore ‘AI for Oceans’, an interactive CodeAI activity designed to demonstrate how artificial intelligence systems learn from data. Through an exercise involving the classification of images of fish and marine waste, participants will train a machine learning model, observe how it makes decisions and identify potential errors and biases. This hands-on experience will introduce fundamental AI concepts in an accessible way, without requiring any prior programming knowledge.

The workshop will combine individual exercises, small-group discussions and opportunities to reflect on the responsible use of artificial intelligence. Participants will also be introduced to teaching resources and guidance on adapting the activity to different subjects, educational levels and teaching contexts, including schools with limited access to devices or internet connectivity. The aim is to enable teachers to replicate the experience with their students during Hour of AI activities scheduled for December 2026.

Through this initiative, UNESCO seeks to strengthen the digital and pedagogical competencies of teachers across Latin America and the Caribbean, fostering a critical understanding of artificial intelligence and its responsible integration into education. The workshop is open to primary and secondary school teachers from all subject areas, will be conducted in Spanish via Zoom and requires prior registration.

This article is related to the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals.
